statement: Locked-circuit external-carrier theorem: if d defect demands in a fixed original graph all have the same two-point outer support {b,c}, then every root choice has base e={b,c} and identical actual neighbourhood K(e). Their matching rank is min(d,|K(e)|) and deficiency is max(0,d-|K(e)|). Root reversals, alternating rematching on existing arcs, demand-cut uncrossing, and random sampling cannot increase this rank. If d>|K(e)|, any saturation must use at least d-|K(e)| distinct actual missing B-edges outside K(e), with graph-proved legal arcs and all augmented Hall cuts verified.
closes: rules out root-only alternating augmentation on locked two-point circuits
rules out reserve-only rotation, uncrossing, and nibble as carrier creation
identifies external graph-derived legal arcs as a necessary input for both round-four survivors
dependency_gaps: M809R4-04 must construct actual absorber outputs outside locked K(e), prove legal demand arcs, bounded overlap, and all-cut saturation from hard graph geometry.
M809R4-10 must prove legal reserve-neighbourhood expansion and codegree control in an actual-carrier-rich hard branch, followed by deterministic cleanup of maximum Hall deficiency.
Neither survivor currently supplies one external carrier on the exact n=14 locked graph.
No composition with the exact outer-A gate, all public hard branches, or the frozen 1/8 coefficient has been proved.
